claim_falsified: One-point exchange stability implies strict self-consistent nearest-centroid assignment even when coincident positive-weight score atoms may be assigned to different cells.

exact_quantities.strict_distance_failure: Rows 0 and 1 have zero distance to both centroids 0 and 1.

verification.notes: All three cells are singletons, so the labeling is vacuously one-point exchange stable under the nonempty-cell rule. Information is positive definite in d=1, but split duplicate atoms prevent strict assignment and deterministic score-only reproduction. Merging the two score-1 rows removes the degeneracy.
